source: Kalshi Trade API AsyncAPI spec (cfbenchmarks_value channel), synced 2026-10-10
claim: Crypto 15-minute contracts settle on the simple average of 60 one-second CF Benchmarks RTI values in (close-60s, close]; Kalshi streams the running final-minute average as last_60s_windowed_average_15min.
hypothesis: Modelling the distribution of the final-minute average (not the spot at close) reduces Brier score versus a spot-at-close model, especially inside the final 2 minutes.
methodology: Run both model variants on OOS_TEST + LIVE_FORWARD markets; compare Brier with window-clustered bootstrap CI.

claim: Our strike_type/floor_strike/expiration_value logic reproduces Kalshi's official result for every settled 15-minute crypto market.
methodology: Fetch settled markets per series and compare MarketInfo.yes_wins(expiration_value) with result.

source: Realized-volatility literature (e.g. Andersen, Bollerslev, Diebold & Labys 2003)
claim: Short-horizon volatility is persistent and forecastable from recent realized volatility; EWMA of squared returns is a strong simple baseline.
hypothesis: EWMA(half-life 5 min) of 1 s CF returns forecasts the next-15-minute realized variance better than a 30-minute flat window.
methodology: Out-of-sample QLIKE loss of each estimator against realized variance of the following window, by asset.

claim: High-frequency crypto returns are heavy-tailed; Gaussian tails understate extreme moves.
hypothesis: Including a Student-t(ν=4) component improves calibration of predictions in the ≥0.90 / ≤0.10 regions.
methodology: Compare calibration buckets of Gaussian-only vs ensemble on held-out markets.

source: Mixed evidence in intraday crypto return predictability studies
claim: 1–5 minute returns carry small autocorrelation in crypto spot.
hypothesis: Adding momentum_60s/momentum_300s as a drift term improves OOS log loss.
methodology: Fit drift coefficient on TRAIN only; evaluate log-loss change on VALIDATION; promote only if CI excludes zero; confirm on OOS_TEST once.

source: Favourite-longshot bias literature (e.g. Snowberg & Wolfers 2010) and studies of Kalshi pricing
claim: Prediction markets tend to overprice longshots and underprice favourites.
hypothesis: Kalshi 15m crypto contracts priced < $0.15 settle YES less often than their price implies.
methodology: Market-implied calibration buckets (market_baseline in CALIBRATION study), clustered by window.

claim: Order-flow imbalance predicts very-short-term price changes in continuous LOBs.
hypothesis: Kalshi YES/NO top-of-book imbalance predicts the contract outcome beyond the CF-based model.
methodology: Add imbalance to a logistic recalibration of the model on TRAIN; test on VALIDATION; must beat model-only log loss.

claim: Displayed Kalshi depth is not fully reachable by a taker arriving ~250 ms later.
hypothesis: Realized paper fill ratio at the limit price is ≤ 50% of displayed depth; the 50% haircut is not optimistic.
methodology: Compare simulated fills with subsequent book deltas; if LIVE data exists compare with real fill ratios.

claim: Fractional Kelly sharply reduces drawdown variance for a modest growth cost, and protects against overestimated edges.
hypothesis: Kelly fractions of 0.10/0.20/0.33 on the conservative probability keep 95th-percentile drawdown inside each profile's limit.
methodology: Bootstrap paper P&L sequences by window; simulate drawdown distribution per profile.
